security_privacy_data_compatibility.evidence: security-data-specialist ran a full, reproduction-based pass. One blocking finding: _maybe_commit_bookkeeping has no branch-discipline check, unlike every other commit path in git_ops.py -- reproduced landing a commit directly on main, and (by the specialist) a detached-HEAD case where a human-authorized reopen is silently lost on branch switch. Three non-blocking findings assessed and found non-credible-risk or acceptable-tradeoff (TOCTOU has no credential angle; .gitattributes collapse is presentation-only; describe_with_live_status's GitHub read is clean). Compatibility: both new defaults preserve existing behavior for every installed repo; derived status is never persisted so no stored data shape changed.

test_quality.evidence: 867 tests, all passing, including new regression coverage for the two bugs found and fixed live during this task's own development (the double-commit fix, the dirty-path-scoping fix). One real gap found: no test exercises a wired function while checked out on a different branch (PR43-NO-TEST-EXERCISES-WRONG-BRANCH, non-blocking on its own, but directly explains why the blocking finding was never caught locally).

findings.summary: _maybe_commit_bookkeeping never calls _ensure_on_own_branch, unlike every other commit-producing function in this file (commit, push, open_pr, mark_ready) -- a bookkeeping commit can land directly on main, on a wrong task's branch, or on a detached HEAD.

_maybe_commit_bookkeeping's return value (the new head, or None) is discarded by task._commit_bookkeeping, so an agent following the documented defer/flush guidance cannot distinguish 'nothing to flush', 'auto_commit is false', and 'a concurrent writer's file blocked the flush' -- and could push without the accumulated state with no signal that anything went wrong.

The function catches GitOpsError from the dirty-path check but not from the add/commit calls themselves, despite documenting itself as best-effort throughout; a concurrent git process (index.lock contention) turns an already-durable state write into a misleading hard failure, and the natural retry is wrong per-verb (record_builder refuses 'already recorded', close refuses 'not in_progress', record_escalation double-appends).

The dirty-path containment check runs against a snapshot, but the subsequent git add -A re-globs the live worktree -- a file written in the window between the two could still be swept into a commit mislabeled chore(codev-bookkeeping), reopening a narrower version of the exact bug this scoping check was added to fix. Both concurrency and security specialists independently confirmed the mechanism; security assessed no credential-exposure angle (gitignored files are unstageable regardless) but confirmed the scoping guarantee is advisory, not structural.

Every test for the auto-commit mechanism runs on the task's own branch (via git_ops.create_branch in setup), so PR43-BOOKKEEPING-COMMIT-NO-BRANCH-CHECK's exact scenario -- calling a wired function while checked out on a different branch -- was structurally never exercised by this PR's own 867-test suite.

describe_with_live_status sounds strictly more correct than describe, with no naming or type-level signal that it carries a real GitHub-network cost describe() was specifically kept free of. Nothing stops a future caller from defaulting to the 'more complete-sounding' function in a hot path, quietly reintroducing the exact per-commit network dependency Slice 5 was written to avoid.

A single-PR task built across many independent, code-additive slices does not fit that model without this kind of manual massaging today.

The accepted plan's stated mitigation for git.auto_commit defaulting to true -- a one-time upgrade notice printed by codev update the first time the default takes effect, recorded as a provenance flag so it never repeats -- was never implemented anywhere in this diff. No code, no test, no mention in the CHANGELOG.
